PR #109 is open: https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/109

Summary of what this task found and delivered:

**Key discovery**: The directive claimed "Task 2 has never been started," but that was wrong. A prior gap analysis + 10-phase plan already existed from 2026-07-25, and its phases 1–3 had actually been dispatched and **merged** into `compliance-tracker` (PRs #559/#560/#561) — real prompt registry/version/lifecycle engines, a compiler pipeline (14 modules), and governance/policy/cost engines with a working approval-gate state machine. Phase 4 (defense-in-depth) has code sitting in an unmerged PR #562. The local reference checkout of `compliance-tracker` was 236 commits stale, so I verified everything against `origin/main` and GitHub directly rather than trusting either the stale checkout or task-status files.

**Deliverables**:
- `ai-os/OWNER_ENGINE_TASK2_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-07-27.yaml` — 145 items (74 engines + 40 individually-classified YCML specs + 31 pipeline/cache/stack/cross-cutting items), each with real verdicts and file-path evidence. Verdicts moved substantially since 2026-07-25: 15 now fully implemented (up from 0), 47 partial (up from 32), 43 not implemented (down from 73).
- `ai-os/OWNER_ENGINE_TASK2_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-27.yaml` — compact 11-phase status refresh, each with repo/scope/verified verification command. Fastest real next step flagged: get PR #562 merged (existing code, just needs conflict resolution + review).
- Fixed a stale status field in `MASTER_INDEX.yaml` that still said phase 1 hadn't been dispatched.
- Registered both files via the existing `record_dispatch_event` writer.

All success criteria verified passing before commit.
